commits.author: Giulio Ardoino
commits.subject: feat(v3): replace the app icon everywhere it is used
commits.body:
Swap the HR wordmark for the new stacked-panels artwork across every surface that
renders an icon, so the phone launcher, the PWA, the desktop packages and the
in-app header all show the same mark.

Each file keeps the geometry of the one it replaces — same canvas, same white
background, same optical size — so nothing downstream needs retuning:

- public/app-icon.png    in-app header, electron-builder targets, Windows taskbar badge
- public/icon-192/512    favicon, apple-touch, manifest (including maskable)
- public/icon.png        @capacitor/assets source for the Android launcher
- public/splash*.png     Capacitor splash screens
- assets/icon.png        kept byte-identical to public/icon.png, as before

Sizing is measured from the artwork that actually reads against white rather than
from the alpha bounds: the new mark carries a much wider glow halo, so matching
raw bounding boxes would have landed it about 13% smaller than the old one.

The Android source is framed tighter than the rest (0.64 of the canvas instead of
0.80). The new mark is nearly square, so at the previous framing the adaptive
foreground overflowed the 66% safe circle and launchers using a round mask cut
straight through the panel stack. At 0.64 the whole mark survives the circle and
still fills the squircle.

Also bump the service worker cache name. icon-192 and icon-512 are precached and
served cache-first, so an already-installed PWA would have kept painting the old
icon until the cache was dropped on activate.
